title: Which faces end up opposite when this cross shaped net folds?
description: A cross shaped net has a column of four squares and one square on each side of the second. The board folds the squares up around the bottom square, then reads off which faces face each other. Keeko's doubt is that the two ends of the column are opposite.
teaching_notes: One idea: fix one square as the bottom, fold the neighbours up as walls, and the last square closes the top. Watch for students who think faces far apart on the flat net must be opposite.

source: A cross shaped net has a column of four squares A, B, C, D f
video_script.why: The child finds opposite faces by folding the net in the mind, because faces that never share an edge in the cube sit across from each other.
video_script.substitution: B is the bottom; A, C, L and R fold up as walls; D, joined to C, folds over the top; opposite pairs are read off.
video_script.anchor: the cross shaped net of six squares, folded on the stage into a cube
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says D is opposite A because they sit at the two ends of the column; A folds up as a wall while D folds over the top, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: B and D, Eigh and C, L and R are the pairs of opposite faces

final_answer.value: B and D, A and C, L and R are the pairs of opposite faces
final_answer.spoken: B and D, Eigh and C, L and R

maths_rules: net: column A, B, C, D from top to bottom; L on the left of B and R on the right of B
B is the bottom; A, C, L, R share an edge with B and fold up as four walls
D is joined to C, so D folds over as the top: D is opposite B
A and C are on opposite sides of B: opposite walls
L and R are on opposite sides of B: opposite walls
video_script.design: One idea: fix a bottom and fold. The net folds on the stage with each pair glowing in its own colour at the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks D is opposite Eigh, because they are at the two ends of the column.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Watch Eigh fold. It stands up as a wall, joined to B.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Two squares far apart on the flat net need not be opposite. D folds over the top, so D is opposite B.
